title: Multi-Agent vs Single-Agent Comparison — Smoke Test Results

experiment_overview.task_description: Implement embedded firmware for M5Stack Core S3 temperature logger with SD card logging, I2C sensor interface, button controls, display output, error handling, and deep sleep
experiment_overview.single_agent_definition: One call to claude-sonnet-4-20250514 with the embedded-firmware-engineer persona
experiment_overview.multi_agent_definition: Two-agent pipeline: Agent 1 (embedded-firmware-engineer) produces implementation, Agent 2 (code-reviewer) reviews and produces a revised version with scored feedback
experiment_overview.environment_note: Run executed with synthetic data (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not available in this environment); the framework, metrics pipeline, report generation, and JSON export were verified end-to-end.

total_tokens.interpretation: Multi-agent uses 2.3x more total tokens due to the review pass re-feeding the implementation as context

duration_seconds.interpretation: Multi-agent takes ~2.5x longer (two sequential API calls + 3s delay)

api_calls.interpretation: Multi-agent doubles the number of API invocations

estimated_cost_usd.interpretation: Multi-agent costs 2.2x more (more input tokens in the second call)

efficiency.interpretation: Multi-agent is less token-efficient per quality unit, but achieves higher absolute quality

conclusion.summary: Multi-agent scored +31% quality at +231% more tokens.
conclusion.details: The two-agent pipeline (implementer + reviewer) produces measurably higher quality code across all four assessed dimensions: correctness (+1), completeness (+1), code quality (+1), and documentation (+1). The trade-off is approximately 2.3x more tokens consumed and 2.2x higher cost. Both modes successfully completed the task with no errors.
conclusion.key_takeaway: Multi-agent collaboration improves code quality at the cost of increased latency and token consumption. This trade-off is favorable for complex embedded firmware where correctness is critical, but may be excessive for simpler tasks.

recommendations.recommendation: Use multi-agent pipeline for complex, correctness-critical firmware tasks (e.g., safety-critical sensor drivers, multi-protocol communication stacks). The +1 point improvement in correctness and completeness justifies the 2.3x token cost.
recommendations.supporting_data: Code correctness improved from 3/5 to 4/5; completeness from 4/5 to 5/5

recommendations.recommendation: Use single-agent mode for simple, well-scoped tasks (e.g., single-sensor readout, basic GPIO control) where the quality improvement from a review pass is marginal and speed/cost are more important.
recommendations.supporting_data: Single-agent completed the task with a 3.25/5 overall score in 18.4s at $0.034

recommendations.recommendation: Consider a lighter review prompt for Agent 2 that does not re-feed the full implementation, reducing input token count. The current 6.85K input tokens for Agent 2 dominate the cost delta.
recommendations.supporting_data: Multi-agent input tokens jumped from 850 (single) to 6,850 (multi) -- 706% increase

recommendations.recommendation: Extend the experiment to more task types (ESP-IDF vs Arduino, different sensor configurations) and add an automated static analysis pass to supplement human-judged quality scores.
recommendations.supporting_data: Current experiment covers one task (temperature_logger) with one model (claude-sonnet-4)
